previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 13th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, managed with anti-emetics. She reported a two-week history of frontal headaches, and an MRI showed no progression of her lymphoma but revealed worsening mucosal thickening in the right frontal and maxillary sinuses, likely contributing to her headaches. No antibiotics were needed. She remained emotionally stable on citalopram, with no signs of active depression. Her chronic right foot pain persisted, and she was discharged with continued gabapentin and a limited supply of oxycodone for breakthrough pain. Anticoagulation was transitioned from enoxaparin to aspirin per neuro-oncology guidance. She cleared methotrexate without renal or hepatic complications and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled in one month.
